title: State

act2.summary: a fourth state, fault, reachable unconditionally, from which only park() is legal

solutions.title: State objects behind a shared transition interface
solutions.tradeoff: Every illegal transition becomes impossible to express rather than merely checked - the compiler enforces that every state answers every call. The price: five files to read instead of one, and a transition that genuinely needs to know about two states at once (not just 'from' and 'to') has nowhere obvious to live.

reviewFocus: Is there still exactly one place that records a transition, or did logging creep back into each state?
Does SlewingState's constructor parameter earn its keep, or is it a sign the interface is missing something the other states also secretly need?
Would a plain discriminated union plus a switch have been safer here, given the compiler can check exhaustiveness either way?
Does the git log show the four guard methods being extracted one state at a time, or one big-bang rewrite?
Is 'park is always legal, even mid-slew' documented anywhere a reader would find it before being surprised by it?
